fields.name: price_seeded_from_ticker
fields.doc:
One-shot guard for the ticker-driven initial price seed. The continuous
ticker loop seeds `price` from `ticker.last` only while this is false AND
the box is empty; it flips true after the first seed OR after any user
price edit (`on_price_changed`, incl. clearing). Reset to false on
instrument change so the new instrument gets one fresh seed. This
distinguishes "never seeded" from "user cleared" — `price.is_empty()`
alone cannot, so a cleared price was re-filled on the next tick (F).
Spot-limit avoids this by seeding only at discrete lifecycle points
(`prefill_price_from_ticker`), never inside the continuous ticker loop.

by the request center on the data source -- no Rust-side timer. Loading is NOT set
here so the panel keeps its current values instead of flickering to "--" while
typing; `run_max_avail_fetch` overwrites them on success.

from V1 `isTPLimit`, the fixed-quantity position flow's distinct

fields.name: tp_limit_price
fields.doc: Take-profit limit-order price (V1: TPSLConfig.tpOrdPx; "-1" = market).

V1 `instType` for the composite — "SPOT" / "MARGIN" / "SWAP".

fields.name: lever

fields.name: order_type

Authoritative user/config writes outrank a remembered default that is

fields.name: tp_trigger_px_type_selectable
fields.doc:
Leverage trigger-px-type (2026-07-25): whether the last/mark/index picker is offered per leg.
Rust-owned classification (SPOT last-only; MARGIN selectable, TP gated by
tp_order_is_limit) — Native renders the picker gated on these, no instType logic in
Kotlin (ARCH-V2 A1). Derived by `orchestration::trigger_px_type` from
`inst_type` + `tp_order_is_limit`; default false.

V2 state for the AttachedTpslSheet (full-screen TPSL BottomSheet).

R-FRAMEWORK conversion (2026-06-08): the framework `#[interactor::state]`
macro supplies the `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, uniffi::Record` derives so
the proc-macro interactor's generated `state()` can return this type at
the FFI boundary (sibling parity: `PureModifyOrderState`). All fields are
FFI-compatible (String / bool / uniffi::Enum / uniffi::Record / Option),
so `uniffi::Record` holds.
